title: Introduce-ephemeral-operator-token-fencing-kms-geo-claim-mapper-and-audit-sparsifier
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Added tenant-bound ephemeral operator tokens with KMS credential fencing, jurisdiction-aware claim mapper for region pinning, and an audit sparsifier to reduce PII exposure in logs. Includes migration tooling and staged rollout plan.
description: Context: We need tighter operator credential lifecycles and clearer residency enforcement for Private/Dedicated customers while reducing audit surface area for sensitive fields. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) Ephemeral operator token fencing with short leases + operator-scoped revocation, 2) A jurisdiction-aware claim mapper that pins requests to region-scoped KMS pools and injects region-consent evidence into decision flow, and 3) An audit sparsifier that removes or tokenizes high-risk PII fields before logs leave the host. Motivation: Recent compliance reviews highlighted long-lived operator tokens and verbose audit payloads as risk vectors. Operational incidents showed operator credentials could be replayed across regions, and audit datasets contained sensitive metadata that complicated external retention requirements. Design summary: - Ephemeral tokens: operator tokens are now minted with a per-operator lease (default 10m) using the new lease-manager service. Tokens include a bounded scope claim (operator_id, allowed_surfaces) and a revocation-hash baked into KMS-wrapped metadata. We added a token-rotation endpoint and an /operator/revoke API for rapid invalidation. - KMS fencing: requests that require CMK usage now consult the geo-claim-mapper. The mapper resolves tenant residency and selects a KMSEngine profile (account/region/alias). KMS credentials returned to the serving plane are short-lived, bound to the request via signed evidence (kms_proof) that includes region_pin and token_nonce. - Audit sparsifier: pluggable middleware runs before audit-forward. It performs a field classification based on policy templates and either redact/tokenize/suppress fields. Classification rules are tenant-configurable and ship with conservative defaults that redact anything matching email/creditcard/SSN patterns. Sparsifier keeps a compact provenance header so downstream consumers can correlate scrubbed events to original tokens when allowed. Implementation notes: - New services and components: lease-manager (Go), geo-claim-mapper (Rust), audit-sparsifier middleware (Python + shared-schema changes). - Minor schema changes: audit envelope adds sparsitfy_meta V1 and kms_proof V1 fields. Both are optional and backwards-compatible. - RBAC changes: Introduces a new operator role template (operator.ephemeral) and updates the RBACv2 policy compiler to emit lease-aware grants. Migration and rollout: - Stage 1 (canary): Deploy lease-manager and claim-mapper behind feature flags; default lease 24h for canary tenants, audit-sparsifier in dry-run to emit sparsify decisions without mutating logs. - Stage 2: Reduce default lease to 10m for new tokens while existing long-lived tokens continue to be accepted for 7 days; enable sparse-mutation for low-risk tenants. - Stage 3: Enforce new policy for Dedicated/Private tenants after 30 days of observability. A migration tool (scripts/migrate-operator-tokens.sh) can bulk rotate operator tokens with audit trail. Security considerations and risk: - KMS-proof binding resists replay because each proof includes request_nonce and expires with the short credential. - If lease-manager becomes unavailable, fallback policy allows a limited number of cached tokens for a grace window to avoid total outage. - Audit sparsifier introduces risk of over-redaction; we include conservative default rules and a suppression-allowlist for compliance audits. Testing and validation: - Unit tests added for lease-manager, claim-mapper, and sparsifier rule engine. - Integration tests run against a simulated multi-region KMS test harness. - Staging rollout included a set of Linear-driven QA prompts (ENG-1274) and a customer canary with two enterprise tenants. Checklist: - [x] Lease manager implemented and documented - [x] RBACv2 policy templates updated - [x] Claim mapper integrated into KMS selection path - [x] Audit sparsifier initially in dry-run - [x] Migration script and runbook added - [x] E2E and security review completed Backwards compatibility: tokens without lease metadata are still accepted for 7 days; audits without sparsify_meta remain valid. Follow-ups: - Add telemetry for sparsifier false-positive rate and a policy tuning UI in Console - Add per-tenant SLA controls for lease durations - Evaluate HSM-backed non-replay guards for critical tenants

review_comments: Arjun Menon: Can you clarify why we chose 10m as the default lease? Response: We tested 3/10/30m; 10m hit the balance between operational churn and reduced blast radius. Observability dashboards included in the PR show token churn at 10m is within acceptable limits.

Sofia Gonzalez: Audit sparsifier dry-run flagged multiple fields for one canary tenant. Suggest adding suppression list and per-tenant tuning. Response: Added suppression allowlist and per-tenant config (examples provided). Also added telemetry hooks for false positive tracking.

Noah Kim: What is the fallback if lease-manager is down? Response: We added a cached-bucket with exponential backoff and a 1-hour grace window; documented in runbook. Also added alerting to PagerDuty on lease-manager degradation.
Security (automated): Please ensure kms_proof cannot be used across tenants. Response: kms_proof ties tenant_id and region_pin in its HMAC; tests added to prevent cross-tenant reuse.
